=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py, lines 709, 719-725 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `_skip_reason` reads `permission_prompt` and the `rate_limit_info` `status_category == "need_input"` signal from only `_summary(session)` (line 709), which prefers `post_turn_summary` and falls back to `external_metadata.post_turn_summary` only when the top-level copy is absent or not a dict. When `post_turn_summary` exists and carries only the limit error text while `external_metadata.post_turn_summary` records an approval prompt, `PERMISSION_PROMPT_PATTERN` never sees the latter and the session is resumed past the pending approval gate. The same single-copy read applies to the `status_category` check on the `rate_limit_info` signal (line 720).
  WHY: The pickup executes the root `.claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py`. A session whose top-level summary carries only limit-error wording while `external_metadata.post_turn_summary` holds an "Approve or deny" prompt is selected for resume instead of being skipped. The template twin at `workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py:724-735` already reads both copies via `_summary_copies()` with the same logic `has_unanswered_request` already uses. The tests at `test_usage_limit_resumes.py` lines 472-493 exercise both cases against the twin; they fail against the root copy, and `test_template_parity` is documented as red until the seventh twin sync. The PR description and progress log (`docs/implement-plan/issue-6102-skip-unanswered-question-resumes.md`) document this as `Status: BLOCKED`, `Waiting on: PR #6112: twin sync (seventh; review round 6 fixed twin-first)`.

- .claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py, lines 719-725 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: _skip_reason reads permission-prompt and need_input status from only _summary(session), ignoring external_metadata.post_turn_summary when post_turn_summary is present.
  WHY: The Claude issue pickup executes .claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py. If a session's top-level summary carries limit text but its external_metadata.post_turn_summary contains a permission prompt (or need_input on the rate_limit_info signal), this runtime copy misses the signal. An old session (>72 hours) is classified as too_old rather than permission_prompt (exposing it to manual resume), and a recent idle session is selected for resume instead of being skipped as permission_prompt, bypassing the approval gate.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "Usage-limit resumes no longer wake a session that is waiting on a human answer" (changelog.d/6102-skip-unanswered-question-resumes.md headline); "The root .claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py follows its workflow-templates/.claude/ twin through the twin sync" (PR description), and the security follow-up #6102 of #5660 whose pre-review-round-6 root copy still had the same defect the twin's review round 6 fix closed.
  Expected change site: .claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py, _skip_reason (new code at lines 716-725 that uses `summary` from `_summary(session)`).
  Evidence of absence: The root copy's _skip_reason at lines 716-725 reads permission_prompt and rate_limit_info needs_input from a single `summary = _summary(session)` copy:

  needs_input = has_unanswered_request(session) or (
      signal == "rate_limit_info" and _text(summary.get("status_category")) == "need_input"
  )
  permission_prompt = bool(
      PERMISSION_PROMPT_PATTERN.search(_text(summary.get("needs_action")))
      or PERMISSION_PROMPT_PATTERN.search(_text(summary.get("status_detail")))
  )

`_summary()` (defined at lines 517-522 of the base copy) returns the top-level `post_turn_summary` if it is a dict and only falls back to `external_metadata.post_turn_summary` when the top-level is missing. So a permission prompt or a `need_input` status_category recorded only in `external_metadata.post_turn_summary` is missed: an old session on a permission prompt is listed as `too_old` (the handbook says to manually resume those — `docs/operations/master-session.md:233`), and a recent one can be resumed past the prompt. The twin was fixed in this PR (review round 6, commit cf39ed38127502690217e8601888d4c46c9c0016) by removing `summary = _summary(session)`, adding `_summary_copies(session)`, and using `any(...)` over both copies; the root copy keeps the single-copy read. The new tests `test_a_permission_prompt_only_in_the_external_metadata_copy_is_skipped` and `test_rejected_snapshot_with_need_input_only_in_the_external_metadata_copy_is_skipped` import the template twin (tests/test_usage_limit_resumes.py imports at module top), so they pass against the fixed twin but do not exercise the unfixed root copy. The PR is held with a `hold` claim until the seventh twin sync (per docs/implement-plan/issue-6102-skip-unanswered-question-resumes.md "Waiting on: PR #6112: twin sync (seventh)"), and `test_template_parity` is red until then by design — the runtime code the pickup actually executes is still vulnerable.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

- .claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py, _skip_reason, lines 719-725 (the permission_prompt and needs_input computation) | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The runtime root copy's _skip_reason reads permission_prompt and the rate_limit_info need_input status_category from only _summary(session) (the top-level-preferred copy), while the twin at workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py:724-735 reads both post_turn_summary and external_metadata.post_turn_summary via _summary_copies(). A session whose top-level summary carries only the limit text while its external_metadata summary records an approval prompt or need_input category is selected for resume instead of being skipped.
  WHY: The pickup executes .claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py. With a session whose post_turn_summary.needs_action is the limit error text and whose external_metadata.post_turn_summary.status_detail is "Waiting on permission: Bash", the root copy's permission_prompt check misses the prompt (it only reads the top-level copy) and returns no skip reason, so the pickup resumes the session past the pending approval. The external-only need_input case on the rate_limit_info signal is likewise missed. The tests import the twin (tests/test_usage_limit_resumes.py:29-31), so they pass on the twin but the runtime root copy remains vulnerable. The PR description and progress log (Status: BLOCKED, "Waiting on: PR #6112: twin sync (seventh)") document this as the next step, and the twin already has the fix; the seventh twin sync will copy it to the root.
